# Mip maps


Textures with flag 8 get a chain of mip maps and are sampled with trilinear filtering, which blends between two levels. The levels are made by averaging 2 by 2 texels, so masked (flag 4) and alpha textures average their alpha as well, which is also what the original did and makes their edges soft from afar. The levels of a texture that is drawn on (`TextureBuffer`) are made again before the texture is next used in a scene. The levels that are stored in a block compressed DDS file are used instead of made ones. A texture with frames (`LoadAnimTexture`, `CreateTexture` with frames) is one sheet, so its smallest levels blend the frames that are next to each other. Flag 8 alone does not use anisotropic filtering, but a texture can be given it with a sampler ([CreateSampler](CreateSampler), [SetSamplerAnisotropy](SetSamplerAnisotropy) and [SetTextureSampler](SetTextureSampler)), which the originals had no way to do:

```blitzbasic
tex = LoadTexture("floor.png", 1 + 8)
sampler = CreateSampler()
SetSamplerAnisotropy sampler, 8
SetTextureSampler tex, sampler
```

See [Samplers](Samplers) for the rest of the settings.
